text: cross-platform-sync.mjs reuses a stale debug Tauri binary: its bootstrap phase rebuilds the frontend but not the Rust workspace, so after editing a crate the harness silently tests the OLD binary (bootstrap 87ms vs 22s). A red-proof looked green until I rebuilt with 'cargo tauri build --debug --no-bundle' by hand. The harness should either rebuild the binary or refuse to run when target/debug/futo-notes-tauri is older than the newest crates/ source.

MCP webview_execute_js kills scripts at a short, undocumented timeout (~10s), so any in-app measurement loop must be chunked across calls; the error is a bare 'Script execution timeout' with no hint of the limit. Documenting the ceiling (or accepting a timeout arg) would have saved three failed runs while benchmarking tab switching.

vitest's config restricts include to src/**/*.test.ts, so a throwaway benchmark or probe kept in the scratchpad cannot be run without either a custom config plus a node_modules symlink, or copying the file into src/ and remembering to delete it. Copying into src/ risks leaving a stray test behind (M16). A 'scratch' include glob pointing at the session scratchpad, or a documented one-liner config, would make temporary probes safe.

Playwright test-results/ artifacts from a failing run are wiped by the next passing run of the same spec, so a failure you want to diagnose is gone the moment you re-run to check flakiness. Consider --output to a per-run directory, or preserving error-context.md across runs.

Uploading MR media via glab: 'glab api -F file=@path' returns 400 (that flag JSON-encodes the string '@path'); multipart file upload needs '--form file=@path'. Also, glab api run outside a repo dir silently targets gitlab.com and 401s — run it from the worktree or pass --hostname.

gate-redproofs' GREEN direction runs against committed state, so a NEW untracked file (a skill's references/evidence.md) makes the agent-docs gate report 'green-not-clean / path does not exist' — which reads as a real broken reference in your working tree, where check-agent-docs is clean. Naming the untracked file, or hinting 'commit new files first', would have saved a diagnostic cycle.

docs/perf/tab-switch-baseline.md told agents to seed a perf corpus by rsyncing ~/Documents/futo-notes (real user data) into the machine-global ~/Documents/fake-notes — two hard AGENTS.md prohibitions in one code block, and parallel sessions share that path. Fixed to generate into the worktree's .tauri-data; a doc that hands out a banned command is worse than no doc.

scripts/perf/tab-switch-probe.js hung forever whenever the app window was occluded: WebKit suspends requestAnimationFrame, so an await raf() never resolves and the probe looked stuck rather than blocked. A QA leg reported the perf claim BLOCKED because of this. Added check()/framesLive() so it says 'frames are stalled' in ~1.2s.

No documented way to bring a dev Tauri window forward for a frame-dependent probe: core:window:allow-set-focus is denied to the webview and OS input automation is banned. Launching a second copy of the same debug binary works (tauri-plugin-single-instance calls window.set_focus() from Rust, ungated) — cost me ~30min to find; now in the probe header + /verify desktop reference.

check-agent-docs.mjs does not scan .claude/agents/**, so a subagent definition (app-qa.md) can carry a stale command, a broken path, or an unsafe technique that every repo gate steps over — the app-qa agent's QA instructions were invisible to the docs gate while it drove real apps

22 skill symlinks under .claude/skills/ pointed into the gitignored .agents/, so every slash command they provided (/tdd, /research, /wayfinder, ...) was dead in every git worktree and fresh clone while looking fine in the primary checkout. check-agent-docs could not see it because readdir() reports a symlink as neither file nor directory, so the subtree was skipped. Prevented by: check-agent-docs now failing on a tracked skill symlink whose target is missing or untracked (added in !211), plus 'just skills-link' for the local links.

scripts/gate-redproofs.mjs revert() ran only 'git checkout -- .' + 'git clean -fd', neither of which touches the index, so a red-proof whose violation only exists once git TRACKS the path (a committed symlink) could not be written: the staged entry survived revert and tripped the cleanliness assertion for the next proof. Prevented by: revert() now 'git reset -q' first (added in !211).

scripts/ci-cargo-cache-freshness.test.mjs flakes under machine load: it fails inside the parallel test:unit:full run (1-6 of its 15 cases, count varies run to run) but passes 15/15 when run alone. Reproduced identically on a pristine origin/main worktree, so it is not branch-specific. It shells out to git in temp repos, so it is presumably racing other git activity / hitting its own timing assumptions when several agents share the machine. Blocks 'just check' for anyone doing parallel work. Prevented by: waiting on conditions instead of wall-clock in that test (M15), or serializing it.

tests/cross-platform-sync.mjs has no per-worktree isolation: server ports are a fixed 4000+ counter and the Postgres reset goes through the machine-global docker compose 'futo-notes-postgres' with a TRUNCATE of the shared futo_notes DB. Two worktrees running the harness at once collide on both. Slot-derive the base port (scripts/lib/slot.mjs) and the database name like scripts/qa.mjs already does.

The harness's FUTO_NOTES_E2EE_DATABASE_URL escape hatch (tests/lib/sync-test-server.mjs) shells out to a host psql, which is not installed on this Mac (Postgres runs only in the compose container), so opting into an isolated database fails with the generic 'Failed to reset E2EE server database'. Either run the reset through 'docker compose exec' with the given URL or say psql is required.

the house main-guard pattern `import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href` throws ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE when the module is imported from `node -e`/`node --eval` (argv[1] undefined), so ad-hoc classification checks against an exported helper crash before running — needs `process.argv[1] &&`; present in several scripts/*.mjs

tests/lib/tauri-instance.mjs and tests/cross-platform-sync.mjs resolve the debug binary as <repoRoot>/target/debug/futo-notes-tauri and ignore $CARGO_TARGET_DIR, so a relocated target dir makes the suite die with ENOENT AFTER a successful 84-second build. Honouring CARGO_TARGET_DIR (cargo prints 'Built application at:' with the real path) would have prevented it; scripts/remote-test.mjs now carries a REPO_LOCAL_TARGET_RECIPES exception list instead.

tests/lib/sync-test-server.mjs shells out to 'bun src/index.ts hash' but nothing documents or checks that bun must be on PATH, and the failure is 'Failed to hash test server password:\nundefined' — result.stderr and result.stdout are both undefined when spawnSync cannot find the binary, so the message names neither bun nor ENOENT. Reporting result.error would have pointed straight at it.

scripts/check-agent-docs.mjs crashes with ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE when imported from a context where process.argv[1] is undefined (node -e / node --input-type=module): its entry guard calls pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]) unguarded. Other scripts in the repo guard with 'process.argv[1] &&' first.

scripts/ci-cargo-cache-freshness.test.mjs inherits the caller's $CARGO_TARGET_DIR: the guard resolves TARGET_DIR from that env var, so with it set the tests inspect a directory that does not exist, the guard reports 'no restored target/' and exits 0, and 5 tests fail asserting exit 1. Green on a normal Mac, red under any runner that sets CARGO_TARGET_DIR (this is how it surfaced). The test should pass CARGO_TARGET_DIR: undefined in its runGuard env, the way it already pins CI_PROJECT_DIR.

tests/cross-platform-sync.mjs dies with 'Could not connect to ws://127.0.0.1:9223' when a Chromium browser (Brave, --remote-debugging-port=9223) is running: the MCP bridge plugin binds 0.0.0.0:9223 successfully because the browser only holds 127.0.0.1:9223, logs that port as its own, and the harness's ws:// connect then reaches the BROWSER. Workaround is to occupy 0.0.0.0:9223 yourself so the plugin scans up to 9224. Would have been prevented by the plugin binding 127.0.0.1 (or the app taking a slot-derived base port) and by the harness naming the port holder in that error.

tests/cross-platform-sync.mjs only rebuilt the desktop binary when it was MISSING, so a second mesh run in the same checkout silently tested the previous run's binary — a #89 fix got a byte-identical false red with 'bootstrap 19ms'. Fixed in this branch by rebuilding when any embedded source is newer than the binary; the general lesson is that any harness caching a built artifact needs a source-staleness check, not just an existence check.

prettier --check enforces BROKEN markdown in docs/spec/sync.md: a blockquoted Gap containing a code span that wraps across lines (`just / journal --dir`) is reformatted so the continuation line loses its '> ' marker and sits at column 0, which stops being a blockquote. A merge that restores the correct '  > journal --dir' fails format:check, so the only way to be green is to keep the broken form. Would have been prevented by not wrapping a code span across a blockquote line, or a prettier ignore range there.

Rebasing any branch that edits docs/spec/*.md conflicts on the committed generated docs/spec/GAPS.md, and resolving it by hand is exactly what M8 forbids — the correct resolution is always 'checkout either side, then re-run just spec-gaps'. A .gitattributes hint (or one line in the spec-gap workflow docs saying 'never hand-merge GAPS.md, regenerate it') would have saved figuring that out mid-rebase.

Write/Edit normalize exotic invisible characters (U+0085, U+205F) into plain spaces, so a helper script whose map keys were literal invisible chars silently became {'' : ...} / {' ' : ...} and a String.split('') destroyed a 1100-line source file. Emitting only ASCII \uXXXX escapes for non-printable characters — and never using a possibly-empty needle in split/join — would have prevented it.

tests/lib/desktop-binary.mjs checks hook markers in one arbitrary index-*.js chunk; after Vite code splitting, every perf-course run falsely cleans and rebuilds 1.4 GiB even though the hooks exist in another chunk. The freshness guard needs to scan all emitted JS assets or use a manifest.
glab API returned HTTP 401 while inspecting MR 209; authenticated GitLab CLI setup or a documented public-read fallback would prevent this
cargo fmt --check fails on widespread pre-existing Rust formatting drift outside the touched module; a pinned rustfmt toolchain or clean baseline would make the required check actionable

perf-course repeatedly reached notes-loaded then drained zero note-open events for its first hash navigation, including after reverting the experimental app change; launcher diagnostics or automatic stale-process recovery would prevent the measurement loop from wedging

perf-course binary freshness guard checks only its provenance stamp, not Rust source mtimes, so local engine/adapter edits can be benchmarked against a stale executable unless another action changes the binary

perf-course can fail after a valid cold-start sample when note-switching receives no note-open event for fleet-pebble; a cold-start-only autoresearch iteration mode or robust event diagnostics would prevent losing the run

command safety rejected cleanup of a mktemp-created probe directory even though AGENTS explicitly permits removing paths the script itself created; clearer allowed scratch cleanup syntax would prevent interruption
justfile has TypeScript formatting recipes but no Rust fmt/check recipe, so Rust changes cannot follow the repo rule to run every command through just; add rustfmt wrappers
just format-check scans sibling .worktrees and fails on hundreds of files outside the active worktree; ignore .worktrees/wtbase so formatting verifies the current checkout only
just arch-gate drift check scans wtbase as if it were active source and reports three false unregistered worktree-slot copies; exclude nested worktree mirrors from drift discovery
The installed glab rejects the common 'mr view --json' workflow; repo automation needs a documented version-compatible way to inspect and update MR metadata.
glab cannot recognize the repository's configured self-hosted GitLab remote, so MR inspection/update fails until the host is configured.

MCP bridge port is fixed at 9223 (not slot-derived like the other worktree ports), and the app binds 0.0.0.0 while tests/lib/mcp-client.mjs dials 127.0.0.1 — any other local listener on 127.0.0.1:9223 (a Brave remote-debugging session here) silently wins, so just test-desktop-smoke fails with 'Could not connect to ws://127.0.0.1:9223 after 30000ms' against a perfectly healthy dev app. Deriving the bridge port from the worktree slot (scripts/lib/slot.mjs) would have prevented it

Fresh worktree: apps/android AGENTS.md says './gradlew :app:installDebug is enough' for Kotlin iteration, but a new worktree has no local.properties and no ANDROID_HOME in the shell, so gradle dies with 'SDK location not found' — and the uniffi bindings are also missing until a full 'just build-rust-android'. Cost two dead-end builds; maybe run.sh/docs should note the worktree cold-start path.

apps/android/AGENTS.md says 'There is no instrumented-test target in check/CI here', but the build:android-native CI job runs connectedDebugAndroidTest on a headless API 34 emulator — a new androidTest written against that doc failed the pipeline in MR !225. The manual needs its claim updated.
Desktop test-hook readiness retries every 2s, quantizing launch-to-interaction measurements even after bridge discovery is prompt; use condition-scale polling for performance harnesses.
The perf harness can focus a hidden macOS Tauri window but cannot show/unminimize it because core window permissions are absent, leaving rAF legs vulnerable to indefinite WebKit throttling.

test:cross-platform-sync fails one rotating scenario per run on branches that cannot possibly affect sync — 'editor roundtrip through real sync' on !206/!207/!209, 'image sync roundtrip' on !207's later run, always 28/29 passed. It made the green-pipeline SHIP criterion unusable for a docs-only MR during MR QA and cost a full attribution detour per MR. Would have been prevented by treating a single-scenario failure as a known-flaky quarantine (retry-once, or an explicit flaky list) instead of a hard red.

check-agent-docs passes on a DANGLING symlinked skill directory: !207 commits .claude/skills/wayfinder and .claude/skills/writing-great-skills as symlinks into .agents/skills/, which is gitignored and has zero tracked files, so both dangle on every fresh clone — while docs/agents/issue-tracker.md tells agents '/wayfinder' exists. The gate checks just/pnpm/path references but never resolves a skill-directory symlink, so a broken instruction surface went green. Would have been prevented by having check-agent-docs stat symlink targets under .claude/skills/.

CORRECTION to the earlier 'test:cross-platform-sync is flaky, quarantine it' cut: the six failures were NOT gate flakiness. Every failing job sha lacked da4a1bc24 (a harness race fix that shipped as one of MR !206's own commits and only reached main when !206 merged). The right procedure when one scenario fails on branches that cannot affect it: check whether the branch predates a harness/test fix already on main — 'git merge-base --is-ancestor <fix> <job sha>' — and rebase, rather than quarantining the gate. Separately the assertion WAS silent-green (deleting flushPendingSave from performSync still passed), fixed in MR !212.

remote-test --doctor reports 'playwright browsers' as [ok] by listing whatever chromium builds exist on the remote (1208/1217) without comparing against the version this repo pins (@playwright/test ^1.58.1 -> chromium-1228). A green doctor therefore promises a playwright run that will actually fail on the remote asking for 'playwright install chromium'. The check should compare the installed set against the pinned revision and warn on mismatch.

A stacked MR's pipeline runs its own branch head, which can be based on a STALE parent: !204/!205 were stacked on !203 before its fix commit 225c28c50, so test:e2e:rest failed there and the failure was attributed to !203 (whose own pipeline was green on the same test). Nothing in the MR view or the job log says 'this pipeline does not contain the parent MR's current head'. A 'stack freshness' check (is each stacked branch's merge-base the parent branch's current tip?) before triaging a stacked-MR failure would have saved a multi-hour root-cause hunt.

Concrete follow-up for pc_0f9cd469b97a (stale stacked-MR pipelines): the check is ~5 lines and needs no new infrastructure. For every open MR whose target_branch is ANOTHER open MR's source_branch (i.e. a stacked MR), assert 'git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/<target_branch> origin/<source_branch>'; a NO means that pipeline is testing a base without its parent's current head, so its failures are not attributable to its own diff. Deliberately scoped to stacked MRs only — running it against main would fire on every MR that is merely behind main, which is normal and would make it noise. Would have redirected the !203 remote-rename hunt to !204/!205 in one command.

The unit 'test' job flakes on CPU starvation when several pipelines share futocoredebianrunner1. FolderTreeView.test.ts's three virtualization tests each mount a 600-row list; measured locally they take 54ms/65ms/52ms (whole file 1.12s), but on CI with 3 stacked-MR pipelines in flight they took 5397ms/3619ms/3408ms (file 20032ms) and one crossed vitest's 5000ms default -> red. That is a 60-100x slowdown, so the assertion is fine and the CPU is not. vitest already caps maxWorkers:4 in CI, so the contention is between concurrent JOBS on the one shared runner, not within vitest. Same run had a test:rust:workspace hang 3870s and jobs in waiting_for_resource. Fixes worth considering: mark these jobs interruptible + use a merge train so stacked MRs do not run concurrently, and/or cut the mount cost in that file so it has headroom instead of bumping a timeout (M15).

axe/idb UI commands return a degenerate 0x0 root for a simulator that was booted headlessly by QA infra (just qa-claim ios boots it without attaching a Simulator.app window in the current WindowServer context). simctl screenshot works fine the whole time, so the failure looks like an app problem rather than a windowing problem, and an agent can burn a long session concluding the UI is unreadable. Re-running 'open -a Simulator' while already booted does NOT fix it. The fix is a full reboot cycle: xcrun simctl shutdown <udid> && xcrun simctl boot <udid> && open -a Simulator --args -CurrentDeviceUDID <udid>. Worth doing in qa-claim itself, or documenting in the /verify skill's references/ios.md next to the M21 warnings.

just perf-course (and every tests/lib/tauri-instance.mjs launcher) trusts the MCP bridge port the app logs, but the plugin probes 0.0.0.0 while clients dial 127.0.0.1:9223 — an unrelated headless browser holding 127.0.0.1:9223 made the app 'listen' on 9223 and the harness connect to the foreign process, failing after 30s with a misleading 'desktop startup failed'; worse, a running dev instance on that port would be measured instead. Derive the bridge port per worktree like scripts/lib/slot.mjs does for cdp/dev ports, and assert the connected peer is the spawned pid

No just recipe installs a RELEASE-signed Android build on a local device/emulator — deploy-deb/deploy-rpm/deploy-ios all exist for prod installs, but Android only has android-native (debug, com.futo.notes.dev). Asked to install 'the prod app' on all three platforms, Android had to be descoped to debug. A 'just deploy-android' (assembleRelease + install, gated on hasReleaseKeystore with a clear message when absent) would have covered it.

just arch-gate's drift scan includes the repository-local wtbase fixture/worktree, so it reports three false unregistered copies and blocks an otherwise read-only architecture check; the scanner should exclude managed fixture/worktree directories or operate from git-tracked files.

evidence.note: drift-check reported wtbase/justfile, wtbase/scripts/qa.mjs, and wtbase/scripts/tauri-dev.mjs as new occurrences

text: just check fails locally because scripts/drift-check.mjs walk() ignores git exclude rules: a nested non-dot-prefixed git worktree (wtbase/) is scanned and reported as unregistered drift copies. SKIP_DIRS only skips node_modules/.git/dot-dirs, so any sibling checkout under the repo root breaks arch-gate for everyone with one.

pnpm run format:check (just check) reports 196 style failures from nested git worktrees: .prettierignore omits .worktrees/, .claude/worktrees/ and any sibling checkout, and prettier's glob '**/*.{ts,svelte,js,mjs,cjs,css}' does not honor .git/info/exclude. Tracked files are clean; the failure is pure noise. Same root cause family as pc_5eb5f10acb22 (drift-check walk).

tauri-plugin-mcp-bridge's free-port scan treats a loopback-only squatter as free: Brave's remote-debugging socket held 127.0.0.1:9223, the plugin still bound 0.0.0.0:9223, and the /verify desktop playbook's documented 127.0.0.1 connection + 'qa-target.mjs port' loop then reach BRAVE instead of the app (qa-target correctly REFUSED, so the safety guard held). Bridge helpers need a host override, or the plugin should probe by connecting, not just binding.

pnpm run test:cross-platform is unrunnable locally when anything holds 127.0.0.1:9223 (Brave's remote-debugging socket): the app binds 0.0.0.0:9223 so the plugin's port scan accepts it, then tests/lib/tauri-instance.mjs connects on loopback and reaches the squatter -> 'desktop startup failed - Could not connect to ws://127.0.0.1:9223'. Workaround: hold 0.0.0.0:9223 yourself so the bridge moves to 9224+. Same root cause as pc_7fac6f19cc66.

A second futo-notes-server checkout/worktree cannot start its Postgres: docker-compose.yml pins container_name futo-notes-postgres, so compose in another directory fails with a name conflict against the already-running one. Workaround: set FUTO_NOTES_E2EE_DATABASE_URL (skips docker compose entirely) and create the DB by hand.

The /release skill fetches Zulip from channel 'notes-app', which was renamed to 'futo-notes' in May 2026 — the API returns BAD_NARROW 'unknown channel notes-app' and the changelog step silently finds zero messages to cross-reference. Also its wl-copy step is Wayland-only (pbcopy on macOS).
just check is red on a clean tree: check:drift and format:check both walk stray untracked/git-excluded dirs (wtbase/, .worktrees/) and report their copies as violations

New TypeScript under tests/ is prettier-checked but never eslint-checked: pnpm run lint is scoped to 'src packages/editor/src', so a test harness written in TS (e.g. tests/corpus/) gets zero lint coverage while still gating format:check.

remote-test.mjs --wait only accepts the equals form. Passing it as a separate argument before the recipe silently consumes that number as the recipe name and dies with an unhelpful is-not-a-recipe error.

scripts/remote-test.mjs --rsync pushes the working tree BEFORE acquiring the remote worktree lock, so two agents queueing with --wait clobber each other: my tree was rsynced, I waited for the lock, the other run rsynced its tree over mine, and my run then executed against THEIR checkout and died with 'Justfile does not contain recipe corpus-type'. rsync should happen after the lock is held (or the lock should cover the transfer).

remote-test.mjs rsync mode runs rsync --delete BEFORE the remote worktree lock is acquired, so a queued --wait run overwrites the working tree of the run currently in flight. The lock exists to stop exactly this class of corruption (a checkout moving underneath a suite manufactures failures that look real), and the HEAD_BEFORE/HEAD_AFTER guard cannot see it because rsync mode never moves HEAD. Two agents sharing jfedora hit this. Fixing it needs a two-phase protocol: acquire the lock over one ssh, then rsync, then run.

On the shared jfedora box I ran a broad 'pkill -f chrome-headless-shell' to clean up my own hung Playwright run; that pattern would also kill a sibling agent's browsers. remote-test gives each run a worktree lock but no way to reap only that run's processes — a 'just remote --kill' (or a per-run pgroup) would make cleanup safe on a box several agents share.

STRONGER EVIDENCE for pc_7610adf57cbd: remote-test --rsync does not just lose a start-up race, it CORRUPTS A RUNNING JOB. A sibling agent's rsync into the shared ~/ci/futo-main deleted a file my in-flight run depended on; vite reported 'Failed to resolve import ../../../factory/driver/corpusTyping ... Does the file exist?', full-reloaded every page, and the run degraded from document 190 of 300 onward with 100+ failures that all looked like product bugs. Two independent 300-doc runs died this way. Workaround: --dir $HOME/ci/<own-dir>. Real fix: rsync under the lock, and/or make the lock cover the whole worktree lifetime.

In a fresh .claude/worktrees/ git worktree, node_modules is absent and 'pnpm exec vitest' from the repo root fails with ERR_PNPM_RECURSIVE_EXEC_FIRST_FAIL ('Command "vitest" not found') instead of a useful message. Had to run 'pnpm install' then call node_modules/.bin/vitest directly. A just recipe for a single test file, or making worktree setup install deps, would save the detour.

Editing a CSS file under src/features/ while 'just tauri-dev' was running did not hot-reload in the Tauri webview — the old rule stayed live and my measurement silently reported the pre-edit result. Files under src/styles/ did reload. Cost a wrong conclusion until I forced location.reload(). Worth pinning down whether feature-scoped CSS is outside vite's HMR graph for the Tauri entry.

GitLab file uploads via glab need --form, not -f/--field: 'glab api projects/<id>/uploads -f file=@path' returns HTTP 400 {"error":"file is invalid"} because -f sends JSON, while --form sends multipart. Hit while embedding MR videos; the error message never mentions the flag.

src/AGENTS.md 'Key Constraints' only warns that layer(components) loses to CM6's unlayered CSS, but folderTree.css and tabsStrip.css are imported directly from their Svelte components and are unlayered too — so a layered rule silently loses to them on cascade origin, not specificity. Cost a debug cycle building a desktop-wide cursor rule that appeared to apply (computed style on .desktop-body changed) while .note-row and .sidebar-toggle-btn kept cursor:pointer. The constraint should say 'any component-imported CSS is unlayered', not just CM6.

The MCP-bridge protocol note in the desktop QA docs/memory says to 'match the reply by id', but tauri-plugin-mcp-bridge replies with id:"" regardless of the request id. A client that matches on id never resolves — my first bridge call hung until the 2-minute Bash timeout. Replies are FIFO; the doc should say so.
glab ci list -b <branch> parses the branch name as a date ('cannot parse ... as 2006') — listing a branch's pipelines needs glab api projects/:id/pipelines?ref=

windows:provision is advertised as the pre-merge Windows check on MRs, but PROXMOX_USER/TOKEN_ID/TOKEN_SECRET are protected variables and only main + ci/windows-smoke-test are protected branches — from a normal feature branch it prints 'Using VMID: ' (empty) and 'Clone task started: ' (empty) and grinds instead of failing fast. No assertion on the empty VMID (M11).

Playwright's page.mouse.click() never moves the pointer between down and up, so the whole editor blank-space/click-off suite can't see WebKit's native selection-drag hijack; and the only Playwright project is chromium, which is immune to it. A webkit project (or a jitter helper) would have caught it.

svelte-ignore with multiple codes must be comma-separated in Svelte 5 — space-separated codes are silently ignored for the second code, so check:svelte fails a cycle later with the warning you thought you'd suppressed

Ad-hoc WebKit probing needs a playwright.config edit: the webkit-pointer project is pinned to testMatch '**/editor-ux.spec.ts' + grep /@webkit-pointer/, so a throwaway probe spec silently reports 'No tests found' on --project=webkit-pointer. Had to widen testMatch and revert it. A second local-only project matching tests/zz-*.spec.ts (gitignored) would make WebKit probing a one-liner.

just ios-native-device failed with 'Could not determine a signing team' — the justfile comment says it 'Reuses the Tauri app's dev team', but run-device.sh only reads FUTO_DEV_TEAM or apps/ios/.signing-team and neither exists in a fresh worktree. Either derive the team from the codesigning identity (security find-identity -> OU) or fix the comment to say it must be set once.

xcrun devicectl device copy to --remove-existing-content true wiped the app's whole Documents tree, not just the --destination subdirectory I pointed it at (Documents/ui-tests/probe). The command also exited non-zero while doing it. Anything driving a device container should copy without that flag, or pull a backup first — the blast radius is not what the flag name implies.

just android-native dies with a bare 'What went wrong: 25.0.2' from Gradle. Cause: the only JDK on the machine is Android Studio's bundled JBR, now 25.0.2, and the gradle-8.14.3 wrapper does not support Java 25 — so the error is just the version string with no explanation. A newly-updated Android Studio breaks the Android build with no actionable message; worth pinning a toolchain/JAVA_HOME in run.sh or checking the JDK version up front.

android-drive tap <label> scrolls the target row to the very TOP of the screen and taps it there, where the status bar swallows the touch — the command reports 'tapped X at 274,11' and nothing happens. Worth clamping the tap y below the status bar inset, or tapping the row's preview line instead of its title.

Targeted eslint on a changed Svelte editor file reported 'File ignored because no matching configuration was supplied'; the repo's lint script intentionally covers only TypeScript, while Svelte validation belongs to svelte-check.
The editor-embed Playwright verification performs an unconditional production Vite build before tests; this is non-obvious when the task permits checks but explicitly excludes builds.
spawn_agent rejects an explicit default agent_type when fork_turns is all, even though the API accepts both fields; retrying without agent_type.

Android native QA build rebuilt Rust and editor successfully but just android-native could not locate a Java Runtime; the Android playbook does not mention pinning Android Studio's bundled JBR via JAVA_HOME.

On the pooled Android emulator, adb input text delivered only PER from PERSIST42 and later adb input keyevent/text produced nothing despite the WebView being focused and served by the IME. CDP Input.insertText worked, so persistence QA could continue, but the playbook's suggested adb text path was not reliable.

Parallel Android/iOS QA agents shared one worktree, but  is worktree-wide: Android cleanup also released and shut down the sibling iOS agent's claimed simulator. The playbook says to release when finished but does not warn that platform-scoped release is unavailable.

Wrote audit output to /tmp/audit-out.txt, then every Bash read of it (grep/head) was denied by the auto-mode classifier while the Read tool worked fine — so finding one summary line took four paged Read calls instead of one grep. macOS has no `timeout` (it's `gtimeout` from coreutils), so a defensive `timeout 60 docker manifest inspect ...` dies with 'command not found' and looks like the docker call failed rather than the wrapper. Two commands wasted before I spotted it. Worth a note in CONTRIBUTING or just not reaching for timeout in this repo's scripts.

scripts/check-qa-input-safety.mjs crashes on import under `node -e` / `node --eval`: its bottom guard calls pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]) unconditionally, and argv[1] is undefined there. scripts/qa-target.mjs already guards with `process.argv[1] &&`. Cost me a detour to a temp .mjs file to probe scanText() while extending the gate.

Process-name pkill has no guard: agents cleaning up their own dev server run `pkill -f vite` / `pkill -f 'cargo tauri dev'` and kill every parallel worktree's processes. M24 and check-qa-input-safety.mjs cover OS-level INPUT only, not termination, so nothing catches it — and the damage is silent, producing false negatives in peers' verification rather than an error.

evidence.note: Three incidents in one hour across six parallel worktree agents, 2026-08-19: (1) ~14:37 `pkill -f 'cargo tauri dev'` + `pkill -f 'cargo  run --no-default-features'` killed peer worktrees' tauri supervisors, orphaning their app binaries — an orphaned window keeps its MCP bridge alive but stops rebuilding, so a peer can conclude 'my change had no effect' from a build that never happened. (2) ~14:41 `pkill -f vite` took every worktree's dev server to zero, invalidating in-flight Playwright runs and screenshots. (3) A settings agent independently reported executing a peer's script. AGENTS.md M24 and scripts/check-qa-input-safety.mjs already name process-name matching against this app as a hazard, but both are scoped to INPUT (AppleScript UI scripting, cliclick, click injection) and to instruction surfaces. Nothing covers process TERMINATION, and `just qa-target` — the sanctioned resolver — has a `kill` verb that agents did not reach for because no rule points them at it for cleanup. Note the justfile itself teaches the pattern: deploy-deb and deploy-rpm both run `pkill -f futo-notes-tauri`, which is safe for a single-checkout deploy but is exactly the idiom agents then copy into a six-worktree machine.

In a fresh git worktree, 'just check' dies on its second recipe with 'undefined' followed by 'ERR_PNPM_RECURSIVE_EXEC_FIRST_FAIL Command "tsx" not found' (toolbar-spec-check). The real cause is that node_modules doesn't exist yet in the new worktree — the error names tsx, not the missing install. 'just check' could fail fast with 'run just install first' when node_modules is absent, or depend on an install check.

glab mr create hides the real API error: on this repo it printed a generic three-bullet 'ensure you are authenticated / MRs enabled / your role allows it' guess-list plus a recovery file, while the same request via 'glab api --method POST projects/:id/merge_requests' immediately returned 'Unauthenticated.'. Reads (glab mr list) succeed anonymously because the project is public, so the CLI looks authenticated until the first write. Surfacing the API status/message in mr create would have saved several minutes.

glab WRITE commands cannot authenticate on this Mac: 'glab mr create' fails with 'Unauthenticated.' and leaves a recover file, while 'glab mr list'/'glab api' reads succeed only because the project is public. There is no gitlab.futo.org host entry in ~/Library/Application Support/glab-cli/config.yml and GITLAB_TOKEN is exported only from the interactive ~/.zshrc, which a non-interactive agent shell never sources. The working path for opening an MR is git push options over SSH ('git push -u origin <branch> -o merge_request.create -o merge_request.target=main -o merge_request.title=... -o merge_request.description=...'), but those are only transmitted when the push actually updates a ref — so an already-pushed branch needs a new commit first. Worth documenting the push-option route (and the auth gap) wherever agents are told to use glab.

verify/references/desktop.md and README teach 'pnpm run dev -- --port N' but pnpm forwards the literal '--' to vite, which ignores the port and serves the slot default instead — use 'pnpm exec vite --port N'

A dev-only override (e.g. ?forceDesktop=1) would make Playwright screenshot loops possible.
